rounds.proof_sketch: Kernel launch: threads_count = min(out_features, 1024). Thread indices out_idx ∈ [0, threads_count-1]. Case 1 (out_features < 1024): out_idx ∈ [0, out_features-1], so out_idx >= out_features is ALWAYS false. Case 2 (out_features >= 1024): out_idx ∈ [0, 1023], and since out_features >= 1024, out_idx >= out_features is ALWAYS false. Therefore both original guard (out_idx >= out_features) and mutant guard (out_idx >= out_features + 1) are NEVER triggered.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the early-return boundary check from `out_idx >= out_features` to `out_idx >= out_features + 1`. However, the kernel launch configuration sets `threads_count = min(out_features, 1024)`, meaning the maximum value of `out_idx` (which equals `threadIdx.x`) is `min(out_features, 1024) - 1`. When out_features <= 1024, out_idx can be at most out_features-1, so `out_idx >= out_features` is never true. When out_features > 1024, out_idx can be at most 1023, which is still less than out_features. Thus the boundary guard is dead code that never executes under any thread. Additionally, the kernel unconditionally outputs 1.0 (hardcoded `output[batch_idx] = 1.0f`), so even theoretical differences in intermediate computation paths would not affect the output.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The boundary guard is never reached because thread indices are bounded by the kernel launch configuration to always be valid. Furthermore, the output is hardcoded to 1.0 regardless of any intermediate computations, providing a second layer of protection against observable differences. Killing this mutant would require either: (1) changing kernel launch parameters to launch more threads than out_features, or (2) modifying model dimensions - both violate the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.recommendations: Boundary guards in CUDA kernels that can never trigger due to launch configurations should be flagged during static analysis. Consider adding mutation testing rules that detect when boundary checks are equivalent due to thread/block dimension constraints. Also, this kernel has a design issue: it always outputs 1.0 regardless of input, making the entire computation effectively dead code - the matmul, dropout, and mean calculations have no effect on the output.
